Tell us how an experiment goes
Thaw collects no analytics or usage data. Permission checks stay on your Mac. The only network calls are the ones listed below, and each has a switch.

Ask us about anything on this page: what Thaw reads, what it writes, why it asks for a permission, or how it moves your items. We are open to any question about privacy, and every one gets an answer from a person.

items.text: Detect the menu bar items on your Mac and where they're positioned. Move menu bar items to rearrange or hide them. Click menu bar items on your behalf, such as when using the search bar.

Lets Thaw update macOS's saved menu bar layout directly, so items move into place without your pointer moving. macOS keeps that layout in one protected file (~/Library/Group Containers/com.apple.MenuBar). Thaw reads it to place items and writes it only when you reorder. Choosing that file gives Thaw access to it alone. Without it, Thaw moves items with the pointer, which takes over your cursor while it works. You may need to quit and reopen Thaw before it takes effect.
Show live previews of your menu bar items. Sample colors from the menu bar to adjust its tint and appearance. Find menu bar items visually when searching.

Lets Thaw keep Live Activities and the camera indicator on the menu bar while apps are hidden. It also stops hidden items from flashing when Notification Center opens. Choosing the file gives Thaw access to it alone. You may need to quit and reopen Thaw before it takes effect.
Thaw reads a 2,560 × 40 pt band at the top of the display. Nothing else on screen is captured.
Crop regions are the exact pixels Thaw reads for each menu bar item. Frames are shown once and never saved to disk.

Checking asks thaw-app.github.io whether a newer version exists. Downloading also fetches it in the background; without it, the download starts only after you accept an update. The release notes shown with an update come from the same server.

Fetches the latest release notes from raw.githubusercontent.com when you open What’s New and keeps a copy for offline use. When this is off, What’s New shows the last copy it fetched, if there is one.

Writes a detailed log to ~/Library/Logs/Thaw/ for troubleshooting, and lists recent item moves below. Turn it off when you are done to avoid needless disk writes. Short crash reports are saved even when this is off.

Each time Thaw moves a menu bar item, the move is listed here, the same record the diagnostic log keeps. Moves happen only when you reorder. The list lives in memory only and is never saved to disk or sent anywhere.

Your pointer never moves: the saved layout is updated and the menu bar re-sorts itself.
